name: Elena Usman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Thanks for making the time. I'm a field researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. Everything you say stays confidential, so you can tell me what you'd say in public and, separately, what you really think. To start, could you walk me through a normal working day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm the office administrator at a parcel depot on the ring road, forty drivers and a warehouse. I do the driver rotas, file the delivery paperwork and damage reports, book vans in for servicing, and handle the holiday requests. I'm junior, I've been there eighteen months, and the payroll side still trips me up. But I've taught myself to build the weekly rota with an AI assistant, and it's cut a whole afternoon down to forty minutes.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How did you get into using AI for that?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Honestly, I was drowning. The old rota was a spreadsheet my manager made in about 2015, and every Friday I'd get it wrong and a driver would turn up on his day off. I tried an AI tool one night at home, pasted in the rules, and it just worked. Now I use it every day for emails, rotas, and checking the damage reports for missing bits.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The first picture is called AI Plateau. I'll read it as written. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say it's a decent tool, nothing magic, which is what I think already. At work I'd keep showing the other office girl how to use it for the boring bits. Online, I don't post much, I'd maybe share a funny article.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, that's a good world for me. I'm the one who already knows the shortcuts, so I keep my edge and nothing gets scary. Tomasz, my partner, drives a forklift in the same warehouse, so we're both fine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep doing what I do. I'd ask my manager if I can take on payroll properly, now that the rota's quicker, so I'm worth a bit more. I'd keep saving, we've got about three months between us, and I'd like to get it to six.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. Quite pleased with myself, actually.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Anything about the depot that worries you, AI or not?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The depot lost a big contract with a clothing firm last year, and they let six drivers go. If the depot loses another contract, it's drivers and warehouse staff first, which means my partner. So it's not me I worry about so much as him.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would losing Tomasz's wage change things?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We'd manage on mine for a couple of months, with the savings. He'd find something, there's other depots on the ring road. But we'd stop the weekly takeaway and the car would have to last another year.

say: I'd call AI a **decent tool**, nothing magic, which I already think.
I'd keep showing my colleague how to use it for **boring bits**.
think: This is a **good world** for me, because I already know the shortcuts.
My real worry is the depot losing **contracts**, which hits Tomasz first.
do: Ask to take on **payroll** properly now the rota's quicker.
Grow our shared savings from **three to six** months.
S0.quote: If the depot loses another contract, it's drivers and warehouse staff first, which means my partner.
fieldNote: She's the depot's quiet **AI expert** despite being junior.
Her worry is her partner's **warehouse job**, tied to depot contracts.
Money is **moderate** and she has a clear target of six months.

steps.text: Ask the manager to take on payroll properly
Grow shared savings from three to six months

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The second picture is called Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the depot should get ahead of it, not wait for head office to decide. At work I'd offer to run a little session for the office. I'd say AI's coming either way, so learn it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, it's a bit scary, because the rota, the paperwork, the bookings, that's all on your list. But I've already done a lot of it with AI, so I think I'd be the one they keep to run it. The other office girl, I'm not so sure about.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask head office about the new routing software they've been talking about and volunteer to pilot it. I'd do a short online course in logistics planning, because that's the next job up from mine. And I'd keep saving, maybe a bit harder.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy. Mostly excited, but with a knot.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You said you'd be the one they keep. What if head office centralises it all?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I'd go to head office. It's an hour's drive, but they pay more. I'd rather commute than be stuck.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What about Tomasz in this world?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Robots spread slowly in this one, so forklifts are probably fine for a while. My partner on his forklift would be safer than me at my desk, which is funny, because I always thought it was the other way round.

I'd offer to run a **session** for the office.

do: Volunteer to **pilot** the new routing software from head office.
Take a short online **logistics planning** course.
S1.quote: My partner on his forklift would be safer than me at my desk, which is funny, because I always thought it was the other way round.
fieldNote: She expects to **survive** by running the tools that take her tasks.
Willing to **commute** an hour to head office if needed.
Notices the irony that her **hands-on partner** is now safer.

steps.text: Volunteer to pilot head office's routing software

Save harder toward six months of bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The third picture is called AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say this is huge and people should be paying attention. I'd tell everyone at the depot to start planning, not just the office. I'd probably post more than usual, which isn't much.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think my job's gone by 2028, and planning jobs too. If AI can do any thinking work, it can run the rota and the routes without me. Then three years later, the robots come for Tomasz's forklift. That's both of us, one after the other.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd use the two years to learn everything about how these systems are set up, and try to become the person who sets them up for small firms. I'd save hard, six months by 2028 if we can, and Tomasz would look at forklift maintenance, because someone has to fix the robots. We'd stop talking about a wedding for now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. I'd be lying awake doing sums.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Setting up systems for small firms. Wouldn't AGI do that too?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Probably, yeah, eventually. But small firms are slow and scared, and they'd want a person to hold their hand. I'd bet on that for a couple of years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the sums look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My wage goes in 2028, my partner's in 2031. So we'd need to live on one wage for three years and save from it. That's tight, but if we don't buy anything big, it's doable.

say: I'd say this is **huge** and people should pay attention.
I'd tell everyone at the depot to **start planning**.
think: My job's **gone by 2028**, and planning jobs too.
Three years later the robots come for **Tomasz's forklift**, so both of us go.
do: Learn how these systems are **set up**, to sell that to small firms.
S2.quote: My wage goes in 2028, my partner's in 2031. So we'd need to live on one wage for three years and save from it.
fieldNote: She sees **both earners** hit, one after the other, thanks to the robot gap.
Her plan bets on small firms wanting a **human guide** for a while.
Wedding put on hold: **family plans** shift.

steps.text: Learn to set up AI systems for small firms
Save hard toward six months by 2028

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The fourth picture is called AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say we've got five years, so let's not waste them. I'd say it calmly at work, because panic helps nobody. I'd be one of the people helping others learn.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, five years is enough to get a proper qualification and move up. I'd go for logistics planning, then maybe into the side of it that sets up the AI. By 2031, I'd hope to be the one in charge of the systems, not the one being replaced.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd start a part-time logistics qualification next year, paid for by the depot if they'll do it. I'd keep using AI every day, and I'd take on more of the planning. Tomasz would look at maintenance training around 2030, before the robots come.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but focused. Like I've got a target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You said 'in charge of the systems'. Is that realistic, starting as a junior?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Probably not in charge, no. But near the systems, yes. I'm good at this stuff, even if I'm slow on payroll.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you give up for this?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Weekends, probably. Studying on Saturdays. And the holiday to see my mum would be shorter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The last picture is called AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say ten years is plenty of time, and I'd tell people to start learning now anyway. I'd probably say the companies will have to train people. I'd be fairly upbeat about it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I'd feel good. Ten years is enough to climb, get the qualifications, and maybe even save for a house. I'd be thirty-seven, which is a good age to be in the middle of a career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd do the logistics qualification over the next three years. I'd aim for a planning job by 2030. We'd plan the wedding for 2028 and start saving for a house.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy at the edges, mostly fine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you change anything about children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We'd probably start trying around 2030, once I'm in a better job. Ten years gives us room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What about Tomasz?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: He'd have time to train in maintenance. Or he could move to something else entirely. He's good with his hands, he'll find something.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028, because it's both of us, one after the other. What would help is training paid for by employers, and a bit of support for households where both jobs go.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Maybe what it's like being the office AI person. People think the one who knows the AI is safe. You're not, you're just the last to go.

headlineQuote: People think the one who knows the AI is safe. You're not, you're just the last to go.
portrait: Elena is the **junior administrator** at a parcel depot and uses AI every day.
She's **pragmatic** and **adaptive**, and built the depot's rota with an AI tool.
Her partner Tomasz drives a **forklift**, so robots matter to her household too.
She's calm in mild worlds but alarmed when **both jobs** go one after the other.
Her plan is a **logistics qualification** and staying near the systems.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028**, because both household jobs go one after another.
whatWouldHelp: **Employer-paid training** and support for households where both jobs go.
